title: Payment failure
text: Customers cannot pay or are being charged wrongly. Money is stuck, so check the payment provider status first. If many customers are affected at once, treat it as a wider outage. A single customer failing at the final step is usually a card or bank problem and is less urgent.

title: Notification failure
text: Alerts or emails are not arriving. This matters more if the customer relies on alerts to catch real problems, and less if it is a convenience. Check whether the sending service is working and whether the customer's address is blocked.

title: Slow performance
text: The product works but is slow. Urgency depends on how many users are affected and whether work is stopping. A slowdown that stops people working is serious. A small delay for one user can wait.

title: API failure
text: The customer's own systems call our API and get errors. Their automated work may be stopping with nobody watching, so it can be more serious than it sounds. Check error rates and whether other customers see the same errors.

title: Password reset
text: The customer cannot reset their password. It is a quick fix, but the person is locked out until it is done. Confirm their identity before doing anything. Lower urgency unless they are blocked from urgent work.

title: How-to question
text: The customer is asking how to do something or where to find something, and nothing is broken. Examples are where to find invoices or billing history, how to change account settings, how do I do this, and I cannot work out where something is. Answer with a help article or a short guide. This is the lowest urgency unless the customer is about to miss a deadline.

title: Billing error
text: The customer was charged wrongly or sees the wrong invoice. Monitoring cannot see this, so rely on what the customer says and the invoice. Wrong charges upset customers quickly, so do not leave them for long, but nothing is stopping their work.

title: Data export failure
text: A customer cannot download or export their data. Urgency goes up if they need it for a deadline, an audit or a legal request. Check whether the export job failed or is still running.

title: Security incident
text: A suspected break-in, stolen login or strange activity on an account. Always handle quickly, even if monitoring shows nothing, because monitoring often cannot see this. Secure the account first, then investigate.

title: Dashboard bug
text: Something looks wrong on a screen, such as a chart or a button. If numbers are wrong, customers may make bad decisions, so check that first. A cosmetic glitch can wait.

title: Login failure
text: The customer cannot sign in. If it is one user, check their account. If many users fail at once, treat it as an outage. People who cannot sign in cannot work at all.

title: Compliance request
text: A legal or data protection request, such as a GDPR request. Examples are a request to see or delete personal data, written confirmation of how long we keep deleted records, a retention policy question, or an audit or legal letter. The deadline is set by law and does not move, so check how many days are left, not how the customer feels. Missing it can carry a fine.

title: Feature request
text: The customer wants something new. Nothing is broken. Record it and reply, but it should not jump ahead of any real problem.

title: Account lockout
text: The account is locked, often after too many wrong passwords. The customer cannot work until it is unlocked. Verify identity, then unlock. Several lockouts in a short time may point to a break-in attempt.

title: Integration failure
text: A connection or sync between our product and another tool has stopped or is behaving wrongly. Examples are the sync creating duplicate records, data not arriving in the other tool, or a connected app showing errors. Data may be going missing without anyone noticing, so find out how long it has been wrong and what has been missed.

title: System outage
text: Our service is down or unreachable for many customers at once. Examples are the platform being unreachable, every member of staff getting a timeout, the site returning an error page, or a total outage. This is the most urgent type because everyone is affected together. Check the status and the number of affected users, and tell customers early.

title: Data loss
text: Customer data is missing or was deleted. Treat it as serious even if monitoring shows nothing, because the damage is hard to undo. Stop further changes and check for backups straight away.

title: Customer says urgent, monitoring says quiet
text: The customer ticked a high severity but monitoring shows almost nothing. Customers often rate their own problem as urgent. Believe monitoring for outages and slowdowns, but not for security, legal, billing or data loss problems, where monitoring cannot see the harm.

title: Repeated contact
text: The customer has contacted us three or more times about the same problem. Repeated contact means the earlier answers failed. Raise the urgency, and look at what went wrong the last time.

title: Contract clock running out
text: A contract promise is close to being broken or already broken. Check the hours left before the promise breaks. A minor problem with the clock nearly out can need action before a bigger problem with plenty of time.
